blockers.reality:
The plan states the trichotomy generically and never picks a branch for any specific fact/doc pair. ADR-0025 Amendment (2026-08-19) requires the opposite: "the plan picks exactly one of three ... never silence. Restating such a fact with none of the three is a plan defect, never a follow-up." A generic conditional defers the choice to the implementer, so the plan itself is silent per fact. Concretely uncovered (canonical source in parentheses):
(1) Package identity `work-audit-refine-red-team` (A1, line 70), canonically the builder manifest in the not-yet-written `adapters/codex/package-red-team.mjs` (cf. `adapters/codex/package-snipe.mjs:33` `name: 'work-audit-refine-snipe'`). Snipe restates its own package name in prose at `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/SKILL.md:8,10` and `adapters/codex/skills/war-help/SKILL.md:18`, and this repo already has the guard shape for it — `adapters/codex/package-planning.mjs:84-85` extracts every `$name:skill` token from the packaged SKILL.md body and asserts each is in an allowlist derived from `config.name`. The plan names an invocation-identity check only inside the package (line 138 "invocation identity", line 139 "alter an invocation to demonstrate those checks fail"), never for `docs/port/2026-09-08-red-team-local-delivery.md` or `references/host.md`, which line 143/157 require to render the package identity, install instructions and intended invocation authoritative.
(2) The diagnostic command, required in the receipt (line 143 "diagnostic command") and re-required at line 157 ("explicit actual-host diagnostic command"). The Snipe pattern the plan says to follow is presence-only — `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/snipe-structure.test.mjs:14` `assert.match(skill, /assets\/snipe-runner\.mjs --request/)` — and ADR-0025 states "A presence check (asserting an anchor phrase exists) or a well-formedness check ... is explicitly *not* a drift-guard and does not discharge the obligation." So inheriting Snipe's pattern here leaves the duty undischarged.
(3) Executable discovery / profile-selection procedure that `references/host.md` (new, Task 1/2/3 Files) would render authoritative; canonical source is `resolveCodexPath` in `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/assets/codex-models.mjs:7-29` (explicit override → `SNIPE_CODEX_BIN` → `CODEX_MCP_NODE_PATH` bundle → PATH). Snipe's equivalent prose (`adapters/codex/skills/snipe/SKILL.md:32`) carries no guard at all.
(4) Local artifact version — line 157 "Resolve the local artifact version from the live builder/source scheme at delivery" reads like the de-mirror escape but names no mechanism and no check; it is ambiguous whether this is de-mirror, a delivery-time manual re-type, or a deferred item.
Neither backstop row covers these: B1 (line 167) is the installed observation/comparison, B2 (line 168) is cross-host alignment.
Out of scope, verified rather than assumed: the "supported profile catalog" is NOT an in-repo literal — `listSupportedProfiles` (`codex-models.mjs:32-94`) queries the live host's `model/list` and `snipe/SKILL.md:28` already de-mirrors it ("Never fabricate a supported-profile map"), and the plan mirrors that at lines 119/72; the Phase-2 SHA and package digest are build provenance, not re-derivable from an in-repo machine source.

needsDecision.claim: Plan §Validation interpretation (line 178): "When a touched authoritative doc restates a machine-readable value, bind it by a discriminating check, de-mirror it to the source, or explicitly add a scoped backstop; do not silently reintroduce stale mirrors." — offered as this plan's discharge of ADR-0025's touched-doc accuracy duty for the five docs the tasks rewrite.
needsDecision.reality:
The plan states the trichotomy generically and never picks a branch for any specific fact/doc pair. ADR-0025 Amendment (2026-08-19) requires the opposite: "the plan picks exactly one of three ... never silence. Restating such a fact with none of the three is a plan defect, never a follow-up." A generic conditional defers the choice to the implementer, so the plan itself is silent per fact. Concretely uncovered (canonical source in parentheses):
(1) Package identity `work-audit-refine-red-team` (A1, line 70), canonically the builder manifest in the not-yet-written `adapters/codex/package-red-team.mjs` (cf. `adapters/codex/package-snipe.mjs:33` `name: 'work-audit-refine-snipe'`). Snipe restates its own package name in prose at `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/SKILL.md:8,10` and `adapters/codex/skills/war-help/SKILL.md:18`, and this repo already has the guard shape for it — `adapters/codex/package-planning.mjs:84-85` extracts every `$name:skill` token from the packaged SKILL.md body and asserts each is in an allowlist derived from `config.name`. The plan names an invocation-identity check only inside the package (line 138 "invocation identity", line 139 "alter an invocation to demonstrate those checks fail"), never for `docs/port/2026-09-08-red-team-local-delivery.md` or `references/host.md`, which line 143/157 require to render the package identity, install instructions and intended invocation authoritative.
(2) The diagnostic command, required in the receipt (line 143 "diagnostic command") and re-required at line 157 ("explicit actual-host diagnostic command"). The Snipe pattern the plan says to follow is presence-only — `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/snipe-structure.test.mjs:14` `assert.match(skill, /assets\/snipe-runner\.mjs --request/)` — and ADR-0025 states "A presence check (asserting an anchor phrase exists) or a well-formedness check ... is explicitly *not* a drift-guard and does not discharge the obligation." So inheriting Snipe's pattern here leaves the duty undischarged.
(3) Executable discovery / profile-selection procedure that `references/host.md` (new, Task 1/2/3 Files) would render authoritative; canonical source is `resolveCodexPath` in `adapters/codex/skills/snipe/assets/codex-models.mjs:7-29` (explicit override → `SNIPE_CODEX_BIN` → `CODEX_MCP_NODE_PATH` bundle → PATH). Snipe's equivalent prose (`adapters/codex/skills/snipe/SKILL.md:32`) carries no guard at all.
(4) Local artifact version — line 157 "Resolve the local artifact version from the live builder/source scheme at delivery" reads like the de-mirror escape but names no mechanism and no check; it is ambiguous whether this is de-mirror, a delivery-time manual re-type, or a deferred item.
Neither backstop row covers these: B1 (line 167) is the installed observation/comparison, B2 (line 168) is cross-host alignment.
Out of scope, verified rather than assumed: the "supported profile catalog" is NOT an in-repo literal — `listSupportedProfiles` (`codex-models.mjs:32-94`) queries the live host's `model/list` and `snipe/SKILL.md:28` already de-mirrors it ("Never fabricate a supported-profile map"), and the plan mirrors that at lines 119/72; the Phase-2 SHA and package digest are build provenance, not re-derivable from an in-repo machine source.
needsDecision.evidence: docs/plans/2026-09-08-codex-red-team-migration.md:178 (generic instruction, sole coverage); Files lists at :116, :137, :153 (the five rewritten docs); :143 and :157 (receipt contents); :167-168 (B1/B2 scope). ADR: docs/adr/0025-drift-guard-discipline.md, Amendment (2026-08-19) — "the plan picks exactly one of three — guard ... de-mirror ... or explicitly defer ... never silence", and the Decision's presence-check exclusion. Precedents: adapters/codex/package-planning.mjs:84-85 (name-derived invocation allowlist over SKILL.md body — a real guard); adapters/codex/package-snipe.test.mjs (derives `$${manifest.name}:${skillName}` and asserts equality against both default prompts — a real guard, but scoped to prompts, not prose or delivery docs); adapters/codex/skills/snipe/snipe-structure.test.mjs:11-18 (presence-only `assert.match` over SKILL.md — explicitly not a drift-guard under ADR-0025).
needsDecision.fix: Decide and record, per fact per doc, which of guard / de-mirror / explicit backstop applies, replacing the generic sentence at line 178 with named choices — e.g. (a) package identity + intended invocation in `references/host.md` and `docs/port/2026-09-08-red-team-local-delivery.md`: guard, extending the `package-planning.mjs:84-85` shape (extract `$name:skill` tokens from the doc, assert equality against the red-team builder's `manifest.name` + SKILL.md frontmatter `name`) in `adapters/codex/package-red-team.test.mjs`; (b) diagnostic command: guard by extracting the entrypoint+flag string from `red-team-runner.mjs` / the actual-host diagnostic and asserting byte-equality with the doc's command block, explicitly NOT the Snipe presence regex; (c) host discovery order in `references/host.md`: de-mirror (point at `codex-models.mjs`'s `resolveCodexPath`) or guard; (d) local artifact version: state plainly that the doc carries no version literal (de-mirror) or add the guard. If any is genuinely deferred, add a legitimacy-complete row to `## Deferred validations (backstops)` naming runner and timing, per ADR-0017's vehicle.

needsDecision.claim: Plan §Build order titles itself '(for /war)' and gives a conditional WAR-dispatch recipe ('If this plan is later dispatched through WAR, pin a run-scoped `overrides.testPattern` …', plan line 111), while binding a hard operator stop: 'Required checkpoint after Phase 2: stop implementation after Task 2 … Only after that attempt is recorded does Post-Implementation Phase 3 begin … Do not silently continue into Phase 3 merely because source tests passed.' (plan line 107, PIN-15 / End state 7). The plan never bounds which WAR invocation modes it sanctions.
needsDecision.reality: /war DOES have an inter-phase operator halt — `## Checkpoint (between phases)` in skills/war/SKILL.md:101: 'Post a phase report … and **wait for the user's go**.' That mechanism satisfies PIN-15 for a default interactive dispatch, so option (a) is partly true and must be named. But the same line continues: 'Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed.' An `--afk` run therefore advances the DAG from Phase 2 straight into Post-Implementation Phase 3 with no operator installation and no first installed Codex attempt on record — the exact silent continuation plan line 107 forbids, and it is unrecoverable for the experiment (Phase 3 reveals the ledger and adapts, destroying the blinded first-attempt evidence PIN-8/PIN-15/B1 exist to preserve). There is no phase bound to fall back on: the Quick start surface (skills/war/SKILL.md:14) is `/war <plan-file> [--working <branch>] [--landing <branch>] [--campaign-ordinal <K>] [--afk] [--ace] [--config <path>]` — no `--phase`, `--stop-after`, or `--until`; a repo-wide grep for `--stop-after|--phase\b|--phases|stopAfter|--until` under skills/war/ returns only assert-issues-filed.sh's `--close-epic … [--phase <label>]` epic-label argument, which is unrelated to run bounding. The plan's own statement that 'the operator intends implementation in another task using goal/Snipe, not automatic WAR dispatch' (plan line 105) is an intent note, not a constraint — it sits three lines above a clause that explicitly instructs how to dispatch this plan through WAR, so it does not close the hole (option (c) is insufficient on its own).

Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed. **Hard escalations (audit-blocked, unresolvable conflict, plan-contradiction) always halt regardless of mode.**' (a PIN-15 checkpoint is none of those three hard-escalation classes). skills/war/SKILL.md:14 — flag list with no phase bound. `grep -rn -- '--stop-after|--phase\b|--phases|stopAfter|--until' skills/war/` → only assert-issues-filed.sh:18,103,110 (`--close-epic <n> --sha <sha> [--phase <label>]`) plus its test; no run-bounding flag exists. Plan lines 105, 107, 111 as quoted.
needsDecision.fix: Settle it in the plan (more than one non-equivalent resolution — operator's call): (i) amend the WAR-dispatch clause at plan line 111 to state that WAR may be dispatched for Phases 1–2 ONLY and NEVER with `--afk`, since /war's sole inter-phase halt is the interactive `## Checkpoint (between phases)` wait and `--afk` converts it to a post-and-proceed — naming that mechanism explicitly so the Lead does not have to infer it; or (ii) split Post-Implementation Phase 3 into its own plan file so no single WAR run can contain both sides of the checkpoint; or (iii) state outright that WAR dispatch of this plan is unsanctioned and delete the conditional testPattern recipe, leaving goal/Snipe as the only implementation vehicle. Whichever is chosen, name the Checkpoint mechanism (or the split) so PIN-15 rests on something mechanical rather than on prose a Lead may narrate past.

minors.claim: "Required checkpoint after Phase 2: stop implementation after Task 2... Only after that attempt is recorded does Post-Implementation Phase 3 begin." — combined with line 111's contingency "If this plan is later dispatched through WAR, pin a run-scoped `overrides.testPattern`...", which explicitly contemplates WAR dispatch.
minors.evidence: `skills/war/SKILL.md:101` (§ Checkpoint (between phases)): the Lead posts the phase report and "**wait for the user's go**. **Under `--afk`: post + `PushNotification`, then proceed.**" Only hard escalations (audit-blocked, unresolvable conflict, plan-contradiction) halt regardless of mode. The Phase-2 install/review stop is none of those, so an `--afk` WAR run advances straight from Phase 2 into Post-Implementation Phase 3 — consuming the "first installed Codex review attempt" that Phase 3 is defined to begin only after. The plan mitigates this only in prose (line 105: "the operator intends implementation in another task using goal/Snipe, not automatic WAR dispatch"; line 107: "Do not silently continue into Phase 3"), with no mechanism.
minors.fix: Add one sentence to the line-111 WAR-dispatch contingency stating that this plan must never be dispatched with `--afk` (or must be dispatched as two separate `/war` runs, Phases 1-2 then Phase 3), since `--afk` auto-advances the between-phase checkpoint that the Phase-2 stop depends on.
minors.reality: In the one dispatch mode the plan explicitly prepares for, the mandatory Phase-2 stop is unenforced under `--afk`.

minors.reality: Nothing at that path exists in the working tree, at the plan's own declared baseline (`origin/codex-port` = 9bc8f676fac1794838f556ed74f2c0d1a9b7bac5), or in any commit reachable from any ref. `ls -d docs/port/red-team-research` → "No such file or directory". `git ls-tree 9bc8f67 docs/port/` lists 10 files, none of them a `red-team-research/` tree or any `.json`. `git log --all --oneline -- docs/port/red-team-research 'docs/port/red-team-research/*' '*2026-09-08-issue-2097.json'` → 0 commits across 3360 reachable commits. `find . -name '*2097*'` (repo, excluding .git) → no hits. `find docs -name '*.json'` returns only seed/ and studies/ files. Every other Evidence-table artifact checks out: both docs/learnings files, all three docs/port files, `skills/war/assets/stage-workflow.test.mjs` (with the lesson's cited `assertStripKeptPromptBytes`/`STRIP_FIXTURE`/`DOC_CAP_PINS` guard examples at lines 643, 506, 783) — all present both in the worktree and at 9bc8f67.
minors.evidence: Scope caveat: the plan says the snapshot is "retained separately from comparison branches," so it may be an untracked file in the operator's local root checkout, which the scope-lock forbids me from reading. What is provable is that no implementer working from any comparison branch (all three of which the plan pins to 9bc8f67) or from this repository can reach it. The plan's own guardrail — "Issue evidence includes full bodies/comments and accounted-for linked artifacts or explicit access gaps" (Commander's Intent) and "never silently claim it was consumed" (Evidence table, last row) — is the standard this citation fails against.
minors.fix: Either (a) commit the snapshot (or a redacted digest) to a path reachable from the pinned baseline and re-cite that path, or (b) replace the path citation with the access reality — "snapshot held locally outside the comparison branches; implementers re-fetch #2097 body + 13 comments via `gh issue view 2097 --comments`" — so the Task 1 PIN-4/PIN-6 instruction derivation "from #2097" (plan line 125) has a reachable source.
